meta.summary: open-diagram treats a diagram like code that must pass its checks, and names each layout problem instead of leaving it for a reviewer to spot.

picks.what: A Python library that lays out architecture diagrams from a short script, measures every label from the font and fails the build with a named list of layout problems.
picks.area: Static-site and design tooling for an Astro site
picks.fitWhy: I already hold my diagrams to written layout rules, and this turns a similar set into checks that fail the build.
picks.caution: Ten days old. Its comparison with other tools is its own. Installable MCP server and skill: review before use.

picks.what: A public ledger of tested hypotheses for running large mixture-of-experts models fast on consumer GPUs, each with its verdict and measurements.
picks.fitWhy: A ledger of hypotheses with verdicts and conditions is the kind of evidence trail I like, even though the hardware is not mine.
picks.caution: All measurements are the author's own, on one rig.

picks.what: Model-specific fused GPU kernels for LLM decoding, written by coding agents, behind an OpenAI-compatible server.
picks.fitWhy: Shows how far coding agents get on low-level GPU work, with benchmarks to check against.
picks.caution: Needs H100 or B200 class GPUs. Benchmarks are the project's own.

picks.what: An open simulator for LLM serving at scale.
picks.fitWhy: Simulating a serving setup before buying hardware could be useful, but I have not seen how close it gets to real runs.

picks.what: A local LLM inference engine shipped as one roughly 50 MB binary with no dependencies.
picks.fitWhy: A single binary is low upkeep, but it is days old.

picks.what: Oxlint rules that keep React code on a design system, with each error naming its fix.
picks.area: Static-site and design tooling for an Astro site
picks.fitWhy: The idea matches my token rules, but it reads Tailwind class names and my site uses plain CSS variables.
